nhan_tran: Nhạn Trận Môn, a war-formation gate of the lake plain: short-skirted marching coats of fine grey-brown felt, close-fitted and clean, with a standing collar and narrow sleeves, over undyed hemp shirts; a plain braided cord belt; a grey goose feather worn in the felt cap or braid by every disciple (the head's is the longest); levy boys and girls wear the same coat new and a little stiff, with no feather until they have stood the line; elders add a square bronze plate on the chest; the head carries a mended grey felt banner with one small goose stitched in undyed wool. Tools: levy spears, felt shields, a drum, a wet hemp cloth for breathing in turns.
le_tuyen: Lễ Tuyền Phái, healers and wine-brewers of the lake meadows: healers wear robes of fine green cloth with a crossed collar and a white sash, and carry a roll of silver needles in green silk; brewers and cellar-folk wear stiff brown leather aprons over green jackets; herb-keepers wear pale herb-cloth aprons with pockets; elders wear fresh plum blossom in the hair after the head; servants and carters wear clean brown tunics with a green armband. Always neat and well kept, never stained beyond herb juice on the cuffs. Tools: needle rolls, white gourds, small porcelain tasting cups, clay jars sealed with red clay, ladles and paddles.
van_hac: Vạn Hác Viện, a zither academy of the pine ravines: students wear plain, fine, clean grey hemp robes with a crossed collar, wide sleeves and an undyed cord sash; left-hand nails are cut square; players who have reached the sixth movement grow the right-hand nails long, hard and pale as plectra; the head wears a thin pale ravine-wind robe once a year; no jewellery beyond a plain wooden or jade hairpin, though one vain elder wears a bright scarlet sash. Tools: long dark zithers on low tables, tuning pegs, silk and thin green wire strings, pine-cone rattles, pine-seed beads.
vu_linh: Vũ Linh Đường, bell-casters and warning-line keepers of the forest roads: charcoal-grey wool coats of good cloth, cut plain for work, with narrow sleeves; every disciple wears the small bronze bell they cast at their first pour on a cord at the chest, unmarked and without any writing; casters add scorched leather aprons black with bronze and burned short hair; hangers and climbers wear leather climbing straps and ropes; wall-keepers carry a ring of small keys; kapok fluff clings to those who pack clappers. Clean and tidy, never ragged. Tools: bronze bells of every size, kapok-packed clappers, bellows, crucible tongs, paper kites and cord, bamboo-paper banners dotted with bronze leaf.
